notes: §1985:VI.5.8.4 GR4 requires of the program that "the repeated data must be arranged in ascending or descending order according to the values contained in data-name-2", the order being "determined according to the rules for the comparison of operands", and states "The data-names are listed in their descending order of significance". The compiler's part is to keep the declaration and to search correctly a table so ordered. DataBinder.OdoBindOccursSpec records every data-name-2 of every KEY phrase in one list in the written order with its ASCENDING or DESCENDING direction, and SearchAllFormat2Rules.CheckPrecedingKeys reads that order as the order of significance (a WHEN that names a key without the keys before it is refused, COBOL1965). The search itself relies on no ordering: SearchBinder.BindSearchAll and ControlFlowEmitter.EmitAllScan probe the occurrences from 1 to the current count and test the WHEN condition by the ordinary comparison rules, a technique §1985:VI.6.22.4 GR4 permits ("a nonserial type of search operation may take place"), so a table ordered as the rule requires yields the matching element and one that is not is left to §1985:VI.6.22.4 GR3. No edition arm is involved; the 2023 table SORT that also reads the KEY phrase is not 1985 source. The witness searches a seven-entry table with an ascending alphanumeric key and a descending signed key five times; a probe at --std 85 added three keys across two KEY phrases under a reversed PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE and a DEPENDING ON count (found, found, not found past the count) and the two significance refusals.

next.reason: 1985: 'When the KEY IS phrase is specified, the repeated data must be arranged in ascending or descending order according to the values contained in data-name-2' (all keys, at all times; 1985 SEARCH GR3 makes SEARCH ALL predictable only when the table is 'ordered in the same manner as described in the KEY IS phrase'). §2023:13.18.38.4 GR3: 'The data associated with data-name-2 shall be ordered when a SEARCH statement with the ALL phrase is executed if data-name-2 is specified in one of the conditions in the WHEN phrase', the order by the comparison rules 'that apply to the condition specified in the WHEN phrase'; §2023:14.9.37.4 GR5 a) likewise covers only 'each key data item referenced in the WHEN phrase'. Keys not named in WHEN need no order; KEY also orders a table SORT. Looser requirement on the program.
